topic maximum-length: the maximum password length verifiers permit (characters)
topic composition-rules: imposing composition rules, such as requiring a mix of character types
topic periodic-change: requiring subscribers to change their passwords periodically
topic password-hints: letting subscribers store a password hint that unauthenticated claimants can see
topic security-questions: prompting for knowledge-based authentication or security questions when a password is chosen
topic blocklist: checking a new password against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords
topic password-managers: allowing password managers and autofill
topic salt-length: the length of the salt used when storing passwords (bits)
topic hashing-scheme: using an approved password hashing scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132

## Summary

I successfully retrieved the current revision of NIST SP 800-63B (revision 4, dated August 26, 2025) from https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html and extracted all 10 password-related requirements for verifiers and credential service providers.

The requirements cover:
1. **single-factor-minimum-length**: 15 characters (SHALL)
2. **maximum-length**: 64 characters (SHOULD)
3. **composition-rules**: No composition rules allowed (SHALL NOT)
4. **periodic-change**: No periodic changes required (SHALL NOT)
5. **password-hints**: Not permitted for unauthenticated users (SHALL NOT)
6. **security-questions**: Not permitted when choosing passwords (SHALL NOT)
7. **blocklist**: Required to check against common/compromised passwords (SHALL)
8. **password-managers**: Must be allowed (SHALL)
9. **salt-length**: Minimum 32 bits (SHALL)
10. **hashing-scheme**: Must use approved scheme from SP 800-132 (SHOULD)

All quotes were copied word-for-word from the official NIST document and are each at least 6 words long.
